testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The brakes will not work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.explanation: If the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, jackknifing risk goes down. The driver can still steer. If only the trailer has ABS, it is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: In cold weather, check and fill an alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from forming in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: The service brake system:

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The service brake system works when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Friction in a brake drum happens when brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction in a brake drum occurs when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal if spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is applied to the brakes. It helps drivers know if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check each slack adjuster after parking and setting wheel chocks. Pull the slack adjusters to check they move no more than one inch from the push rod. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air to use the brakes several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air to use the brakes several times if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air so the brakes can still work several times if the compressor fails.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake, as it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parked. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and temperatures are below freezing.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary tanks. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep hill, what is the best way to use your brakes?

options.text: Use the brakes continuously all the way down.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this cycle as you go down the hill.
Use the brakes only near the bottom of the hill.
Press the brake pedal with steady pressure all the way down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this cycle as you go down the hill.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use the engine to help slow your vehicle. Apply the brakes just enough to feel the vehicle slow down. Release the brakes once you reach about 5 mph below your target safe speed. Repeat this process as you descend.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking.
To stop ice from forming in the brake system.
To keep people from breathing the air in the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems use an alcohol evaporator. This device adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil that build up. If water and oil stay in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?
questions.explanation: A low air pressure warning signal must come on when tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: What color are ABS warning lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lamps.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve is located in the tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
Do not work well on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS is added to a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not change how well the brakes work. ABS activates when you press the brake pedal hard to keep the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when the spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What color are the malfunction lamps on vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps. These lamps alert you when the ABS is not working. Know where your vehicle's lamp is located before you drive.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, what happens?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake drum tightens onto the axle.
The brake lining presses against the wheel.
Air is released from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what component do both systems share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor fails, neither brake system will work properly.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking power.
Work in addition to other braking systems without reducing braking power.
Do not work well on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work in addition to other braking systems without reducing braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS is extra equipment that works with your normal braking system. It does not reduce braking power. ABS only turns on when your wheels are about to lock up.
